# Levantine Arabic: a spoken flashcard deck

Survival phrases in **Levantine Arabic (Shami)** - the dialect of
Damascus, Beirut, Amman and Jerusalem. Every card speaks: the clips
were synthesized once with a text-to-speech API (an Arabic voice,
Maryam) and snapshotted into this document as data URIs, so the deck
plays fully offline - a document never fetches anything at render
time. The deck opens straight into **Match** - the Duolingo flow:
press a clip on the left, then its word on the right.

The synthesized voice reads standard Arabic (MSA) phonology - e.g.
قديش comes out "qadīsh", not the Levantine "addesh". For a true Shami
pronunciation, click the deck's label, then use the mic button on any
card row to record your own voice - Alt-click the play button to
re-record. Recordings land on the card as a data URI, so they travel
with the file.

Each clip lives in its own `::: audio` block and is referenced from
its card by id (`@marhaba`) - record once, reference from many cards.

::: flashcards {#levantine-basics}
title: "Levantine basics (Shami)"
card: "مرحبا" | "marhaba - hello" | @marhaba
card: "كيفك" | "kifak - how are you (to a man)" | @kifak
card: "شو" | "shu - what" | @shu
card: "قديش" | "qaddesh - how much / how long" | @qaddesh
card: "شكرا" | "shukran - thanks" | @shukran
card: "مع السلامة" | "ma' al-salamé - goodbye" | @salam
card: "إن شاء الله" | "inshallah - God willing" | @inshallah
card: "حبيبي" | "habibi - my dear (to a man)" | @habibi
:::

The front of each card is Arabic script and right-aligns on its own -
direction is typography, derived from the text, not stored in the file.
Edit any card's front or back right in the deck, or hand-type a new
`card:` line - pick your own words and record them with the mic. Grades
from studying live in this browser only, never in the Markdown.
